title: 96. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Dividing a Quantity in a Given Ratio
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Dividing a Quantity in a Two-Part Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine the larger share when a quantity is divided in a given two-part ratio.
questions.question: Divide \(60\) in the ratio \(2:3\). What is the larger share?
questions.explanation: The ratio \(2:3\) has \(2+3=5\) equal parts. One part is \(60 \div 5 = 12\). The two shares are \(2 \times 12 = 24\) and \(3 \times 12 = 36\). The larger share is \(36\).
questions.hint: Add the terms of the ratio to find the total number of equal parts.

questions.concept: Dividing a Quantity in a Two-Part Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine the smaller share when a quantity is divided in a given two-part ratio.
questions.question: Divide \(45\text{ kg}\) in the ratio \(4:5\). What is the smaller share?
questions.explanation: The ratio \(4:5\) has \(4+5=9\) equal parts. One part is \(45 \div 9 = 5\text{ kg}\). The two shares are \(4 \times 5 = 20\text{ kg}\) and \(5 \times 5 = 25\text{ kg}\). The smaller share is \(20\text{ kg}\).
questions.hint: Find the value of one equal part first, then multiply by the smaller ratio term.

questions.concept: Dividing a Quantity in a Three-Part Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine the middle share when a quantity is divided in a given three-part ratio.
questions.question: Divide \(72\text{ cm}\) in the ratio \(1:2:3\). What is the middle share?
questions.explanation: The ratio \(1:2:3\) has \(1+2+3=6\) equal parts. One part is \(72 \div 6 = 12\text{ cm}\). The three shares are \(1 \times 12 = 12\text{ cm}\), \(2 \times 12 = 24\text{ cm}\), and \(3 \times 12 = 36\text{ cm}\). The middle share is \(24\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Add all three ratio terms, then identify the share corresponding to the middle term.

questions.concept: Finding the First Share from a Given Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine the first share when a quantity is divided in a given two-part ratio.
questions.question: Divide \(80\) in the ratio \(3:5\). What is the first share?
questions.explanation: The ratio \(3:5\) has \(3+5=8\) equal parts. One part is \(80 \div 8 = 10\). The first share corresponds to the first ratio term, so it is \(3 \times 10 = 30\).
questions.hint: Use the first term of the ratio to find the first share after determining the value of one part.

questions.concept: Finding the Total from a Given Share
questions.learningObjective: Determine the total quantity when a smaller share and a ratio are given.
questions.question: A sum is divided in the ratio \(2:5\). The smaller share is \(18\). What is the total sum?
questions.explanation: The smaller share corresponds to \(2\) parts. Since \(2\) parts equal \(18\), one part is \(18 \div 2 = 9\). The ratio \(2:5\) has \(2+5=7\) parts in total, so the total sum is \(7 \times 9 = 63\).
questions.hint: Use the smaller share to find the value of one equal part, then multiply by the total number of parts.

questions.concept: Finding the Larger Share from a Given Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine the larger share when a length is divided in a given two-part ratio.
questions.question: A length of \(96\text{ cm}\) is divided in the ratio \(5:7\). What is the larger share?
questions.explanation: The ratio \(5:7\) has \(5+7=12\) equal parts. One part is \(96 \div 12 = 8\text{ cm}\). The larger share corresponds to \(7\) parts, so it is \(7 \times 8 = 56\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Identify which ratio term represents the larger share, then multiply the value of one part by that term.

questions.concept: Dividing a Quantity in a Three-Part Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine the largest share when a quantity is divided in a given three-part ratio.
questions.question: Divide \(150\) in the ratio \(4:6:5\). What is the largest share?
questions.explanation: The ratio \(4:6:5\) has \(4+6+5=15\) equal parts. One part is \(150 \div 15 = 10\). The three shares are \(4 \times 10 = 40\), \(6 \times 10 = 60\), and \(5 \times 10 = 50\). The largest share is \(60\).
questions.hint: Compare the ratio terms to identify which share will be largest, then calculate that share.

questions.concept: Dividing a Quantity in a Three-Part Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine the largest share when a total is divided in a given three-part ratio.
questions.question: Three people share \(240\) in the ratio \(1:2:3\). What is the largest share?
questions.explanation: The ratio \(1:2:3\) has \(1+2+3=6\) equal parts. One part is \(240 \div 6 = 40\). The three shares are \(1 \times 40 = 40\), \(2 \times 40 = 80\), and \(3 \times 40 = 120\). The largest share is \(120\).
questions.hint: Add the ratio terms to find the total number of equal parts, then calculate the share for the largest term.

questions.concept: Finding the Smaller Share from the Larger Share
questions.learningObjective: Determine the smaller share when a larger share and a two-part ratio are given.
questions.question: A quantity is divided in the ratio \(3:4\). If the larger share is \(48\), what is the smaller share?
questions.explanation: The larger share corresponds to \(4\) parts. Since \(4\) parts equal \(48\), one part is \(48 \div 4 = 12\). The smaller share corresponds to \(3\) parts, so it is \(3 \times 12 = 36\).
questions.hint: Use the larger share to find the value of one equal part, then multiply by the smaller ratio term.

questions.concept: Difference Between Shares in a Three-Part Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine the difference between the largest and smallest shares when a quantity is divided in a given three-part ratio.
questions.question: Divide \(180\) in the ratio \(2:3:4\). What is the difference between the largest share and the smallest share?
questions.explanation: The ratio \(2:3:4\) has \(2+3+4=9\) equal parts. One part is \(180 \div 9 = 20\). The three shares are \(2 \times 20 = 40\), \(3 \times 20 = 60\), and \(4 \times 20 = 80\). The largest share is \(80\) and the smallest share is \(40\), so the difference is \(80-40=40\).
questions.hint: Calculate all three shares first, then subtract the smallest share from the largest share.
